Fix error_call leak in duckplyr_expand_across and rel_try return
description:
### `error_call  in `` duckplyr_expand_across()`

`duckplyr_expand_across()` passed `error_call` to `quo_eval_fns()` and `duckplyr_across_setup()` but had no `error_call` formal. duckplyr imports all of rlang, so the name resolved to rlang's `error_call()` function. Every error raised while expanding `across()` got a function where a call or environment is required, so users saw an internal error instead of the real one. Calling tidyselect with the leaked value shows the failure:

```r
eval_select(expr(zzz), data = df, error_call = rlang::error_call)
#> Error in `abort()` at vctrs/R/subscript.R:150:3:
#> ! `call` must be a call or environment, not a function.
```

The function now takes `error_call` with a `caller_env()` default, and `rel_translate_dots_summarise()` passes its call through

```r
test_duckplyr_expand_across(tibble(x = 0, y = 0), across(zzz, mean))
#> Error: Can't select columns that don't exist.
#> x Column `zzz` doesn't exist.
```

### `rel_try()` returns the message function in dplyr mode

`rel_try()` in assigned the fallback reason to message only inside `if (!dplyr_mode)` but returned it on both paths. In dplyr mode message was never assigned, so the return value was `base::message`, the function, and callers storing the fallback reason got that instead of the reason string. 

Found during my most recent [ry](https://github.com/sims1253/ry) audit.

title: ci: Document with a patched roxygen2 that keeps the sentence gap
description:
Split out of #955 so it can be decided on its own. It branches from `main` rather than from that chain, so the two do not depend on each other in either direction.

commonmark discards the whitespace a line break stands for. roxygen2 turns every softbreak into a bare newline, so the `.Rd` carries a line break with nothing after it and `Rd2txt()` renders it as a single space. Prose written one sentence per line therefore comes out single-spaced, while the same words wrapped to a fixed width with two spaces after the period keep the gap. Only the text renderer is affected — `Rd2HTML()` and `Rd2latex()` differ by whitespace that HTML and TeX collapse, and LaTeX applies its own sentence spacing regardless — but text is what `?topic` shows.

A new composite action, `.github/workflows/roxygen2-fork`, installs roxygen2 from upstream with the `R/` part of `krlmlr/roxygen2@f-sentence-spacing` applied on top, and `R-CMD-check.yaml` runs it immediately before the Roxygenize step. It shallow-clones upstream, fetches the branch, computes the diff against their merge base restricted to `R/`, and applies it with `git apply --3way`. Restricting to `R/` means an unrelated upstream change to a test fixture cannot fail the documentation step. It aborts if the patch is empty or does not apply, rather than silently installing an unpatched build, and afterwards asserts that what it installed really carries the patch.

`Config/roxygen2/version` becomes `8.1.0.9100`. The `.9100` suffix distinguishes a patched build from upstream's own `.9000` development builds; if upstream moves, the `x.y.z` part follows it and the suffix stays. `DESCRIPTION` is DCF and cannot carry a comment line, so the explanation lives in a `Config/cynkra/roxygen2` field.

`man/` is not committed here. CI regenerates it, so merging this is what produces the updated `.Rd` files, and the diff stays reviewable.

The roxygen2 side is `krlmlr/roxygen2#8`, on the fork, not yet filed with r-lib. It is deliberately narrow: mid-sentence breaks are untouched, links are unaffected, and two guards keep it from firing wrongly — an abbreviation list so a line ending in `e.g.` or `et al.` does not gain a mid-sentence gap, and a fix for a determinism bug where a line starting with `\doi{}` or `\code{}` gained or lost its gap at random.

title: ci: Survive an archived CRAN package, cache revdep compiles
description:
Syncs the CI kit from cynkratemplate: https://github.com/cynkra/cynkratemplate/pull/112 and https://github.com/cynkra/cynkratemplate/pull/113, both merged. Every file here is byte-identical to the template, and the same changes are already on `main` in the 19 packages that take the kit directly.

### An archived CRAN package must not fail the dependency solve

`needs: website` reaches pak as a dependency *type* (`lockfile_create(dependencies = "Config/Needs/website")`), and a dependency type resolves all-or-nothing: one entry that no repository carries fails the whole solve, before a single check runs. That is what happened in r-dbi/DBI when CRAN archived `adbi` and `RPresto` on 2026-09-11 — every check run died in the smoke test. No pak parameter reaches inside a dependency type: `?ignore-unavailable` is honoured for soft dependencies only, and `pkg=?ignore` drops the package even when it is available. So the new `get-website` action resolves the field itself and hands pak refs instead — an `owner/repo` entry stays as it is and stays strict, a plain name the configured repositories carry is kept, and the rest is dropped with a warning in the job log. Nothing leaves `DESCRIPTION`, so a package that returns to CRAN is picked up again by the next run.

### Install an archived dependency from where it still lives

`R CMD check` reads `Additional_repositories` to confirm a dependency outside CRAN and Bioconductor is obtainable, but it never installs from it, and neither does pak, which reads `repos` alone. The new step installs a dependency only when it is still missing after the pak solve *and* no configured repository carries it at all, so anything CRAN still has stays with CRAN and a released dependency is never swapped for an r-universe development snapshot. Best effort by design: a failure leaves the check running with one fewer optional dependency, exactly as `=?ignore-build-errors` does in `Config/gha/extra-packages`.

### A shard-wide ccache for the revdep checks

Carried into the kit from https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-r/pull/2691, where it is already running. `revdep4/queue.sh` keeps one ccache directory for the whole shard, and `revdepx/check-half.sh` mounts it into every check container with `/usr/lib/ccache` on the container's `PATH`. The two halves of a revdep compile the same sources minutes apart — only the package under test in `lib-half` differs — and both halves see identical paths inside the container, so the second half hits on everything that does not depend on the package under test, and misses on exactly the objects whose headers really do differ, because what ccache hashes is the preprocessed source. The comparison the two halves exist to make is not weakened; it just stops paying twice for the parts that were never different. `REVDEPX_CCACHE_DIR=` empty turns it off. These workflows run on a schedule and on dispatch, so this part is not exercised by this PR's own checks.

### Effect here

`Config/Needs/website` in this package lists `dbplyr` and `rmarkdown` as plain names alongside `tidyverse/tidytemplate`. Both are on CRAN today, so both are kept and nothing changes; were either archived, the website build would lose that one package instead of the whole run failing. There is no `Additional_repositories` field, so the second change is inert here.

title: Support sort = TRUE in count()
description:
## Summary

- Removes the `sort = TRUE` drop-out from `count.duckplyr_df()` and adds a native `rel_order()` call: descending by count, with grouping columns as ascending tiebreakers. This reproduces dplyr's observed output (dplyr achieves the same ordering implicitly via grouped `summarise()` plus a stable `arrange()`).

- Reworks the weighted-count aggregate to `COALESCE(SUM(wt), 0)` so that all-NA weights yield `0`, matching `dplyr::tally_n()`'s `sum(wt, na.rm = TRUE)`. The previous `rel_translate(sum(wt, na.rm = TRUE))` path produced `NA` here because DuckDB's `SUM` over all-NULL returns NULL. Covered by the "matches dplyr for all-NA weighted counts" test.

- Captures `wt` with `compat_wt(enquo(wt), env = dplyr, user_env = caller_env())` to preserve dplyr's bare-`n` deprecation back-compat path.

- Regenerates `man/count.duckplyr_df.Rd` and `patch/count.patch` via `tools/02-duckplyr_df-methods.R`.

## Test plan

New tests in `tests/testthat/test-count-sort.R` cover:

- [x] Basic descending order
- [x] Works under `DUCKPLYR_FORCE = TRUE`
- [x] Ties broken by grouping columns
- [x] Multiple grouping columns
- [x] Weighted counts (`wt = w`)
- [x] Custom `name = "total"`
- [x] All-NA weights match `dplyr::count(..., sort = TRUE)` output
- [x] Empty inputs
- [x] Grouped data (preserves `group_vars()`)

`devtools::check()` passes locally aside from two pre-existing fallback snapshot drifts (`summarize()` and `strftime()`) that are present on `main` as well and unrelated to this change.

title: docs: make the `dd$` escape hatch discoverable
description:
The `dd$fun(...)` escape hatch is a purely syntactic passthrough recognized by the translator: there is no `dd` object, so `?dd`, `duckplyr::dd`, and `ls("package:duckplyr")` all come up empty even though it works. That makes it easy to conclude, wrongly, that the feature is absent.

- duckdb.Rmd: state explicitly that `dd` is not an object and needs no package, that introspection won't reveal it, and that the optional dd package is what provides a real `dd` object, `?dd`, and autocomplete.
- limits.Rmd: at the point where untranslatable functions are discussed, point to the `dd$` escape hatch as the way to reach the DuckDB function directly (e.g. dd$var_samp() for dplyr's untranslated var()).

Docs-only: the "Can't translate function" abort message is intentionally left unchanged because it is recorded verbatim in the fallback telemetry (telemetry.R uses conditionMessage), so a hint there would pollute that stream and the translation-prioritization analysis keyed on it.

title: ci: Fix continuous benchmark (touchstone) workflow
description:
The continuous benchmark workflow could not run to completion. Three independent issues, all fixed here:

- `touchstone/script.R` and its data-generation helpers use `qs2`, `pkgload`, and `fs`, but the `receive` action never installs them. `qs2` is declared under `Enhances` (not installed by default) and `pkgload`/`fs` are undeclared, so `qs2::qs_read()` and the data-prep scripts fail. Install them via `extra-packages`.

- `tools/31-tpch-load-qs.R` cached the TPC-H tables as lazy, DuckDB-backed `duckplyr_df` objects. qs2 round-trips them into materialized frames that keep the `duckplyr_df` class and explicit row names, so the benchmark's `as_duckdb_tibble()` aborts with "Need data frame without row names to convert to relational". Collect to plain tibbles before saving.

- The `comment` workflow posts a PR comment and sets a commit status but declared no permissions, which fails under a read-only default `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Grant `pull-requests: write` and `statuses: write`.

Verified locally end to end: generate scale-factor TPC-H data, cache via qs2, reload, convert with `as_duckdb_tibble()`, and run all 22 TPC-H benchmark queries.

title: compat: `as_tbl()` attach finalizer to `lazy_query`, not `tbl`, for compatibility with dbplyr 2.6.0
description:
(Claude analysis follows, needed for dbplyr 2.6.0 release)

`as_tbl()` currently anchors the temp-view finalizer to the top-level tbl:

```r
out <- dplyr::tbl(con, name)
attr(out, "duckplyr_scope_guard") <- scope_guard
out
```

This relies on attributes surviving every dbplyr verb. Today they happen to — verbs mutate in place (`out$lazy_query <- ...`), which preserves attributes by R copy semantics — but it's not a contract, and it already fails in cases like joins (where the RHS tbl is consumed, dropping any `attr(y, ...)`) and any verb that rebuilds via `dplyr::make_tbl()`. The cascading effect is visible in dbplyr's 2.6.0 revdep run: osdc breaks with `Table as_tbl_duckplyr_XXX does not exist` because GC reclaims the guard before `collect()` runs.

The fix is one line — anchor to the `lazy_query` instead:

```r
out <- dplyr::tbl(con, name)
attr(out$lazy_query, "duckplyr_scope_guard") <- scope_guard
out
```

The lazy_query tree is the durable spine of a dbplyr tbl: every verb wraps the prior query as `$x` of the new one, and joins retain both sides as `x_lq` / `y_lq`. So the root node (and the attribute) stays GC-reachable for the lifetime of any derivative tbl, including across joins where both inputs came from `as_tbl()`. Verified empirically against current dbplyr `main`: the finalizer fires at the right moment after mutate / filter / head / collect chains.

title: Add `anyNA()` translation support
description:
`anyNA(x)` failed with "Can't translate function `anyNA()`" despite `any(is.na(x))` working identically. The two forms should be interchangeable.

## Changes

- **New DuckDB macro**: `"anyNA" = "(x) AS (bool_or(x IS NULL))"` — direct SQL equivalent
- **Function registration**: `"anyNA" = "base"` in `rel_find_packages()`
- **Translation handler** in `rel_translate_lang()` switch: validates args, rejects `recursive = TRUE` and window function contexts, returns the translated expression
- **Docs**: added `anyNA()` to `vignettes/limits.Rmd` supported functions list

```r
test_dat <- duckdb_tibble(a = c(1, 2, NA), .prudence = "stingy")

# Previously errored with "Can't translate function `anyNA()`"
summarize(test_dat, anyNA(a), .by = a)

title: feat: Enable `across()` translation for primitive functions such as `sum()`
description:
Closes #906.

`across()` with primitive functions (`sum`, `min`, `max`) failed to translate in duckplyr because primitives return `NULL` from `environment()`, causing `fn_to_expr()` to fall through and return the raw function object — which then triggered the "can't translate spliced function" bail-out path.

## Changes

- **`R/duckplyr-across.R`**: In `fn_to_expr()`, detect primitive functions (`is.primitive(fn)` with `NULL` environment) and substitute `getNamespace("base")`, allowing the existing hash-based namespace export lookup to resolve them to `base::sum`, `base::min`, `base::max` expressions that the translation layer already handles.

- **`tests/testthat/_snaps/duckplyr-across.md`**: Updated snapshots for the existing primitive function tests — `across(x:y, sum/min/max)` now expand correctly instead of returning `NULL`.

```r
d <- as_duckdb_tibble(penguins, prudence = "stingy")

# Previously errored: "Can't translate function `across()`"
d |> summarize(across(bill_len:body_mass, sum), .by = species)
#> # A duckplyr data frame: 5 variables
#>   species   bill_len bill_dep flipper_len body_mass
#>   ...
```

title: fix: Filter write-only options before passing to read functions in `compute_parquet()` and `compute_csv()`
description:
`compute_parquet()` and `compute_csv()` were forwarding all user-provided options to both the write step and the subsequent read step. Write-only options like `compression_level` are not valid parameters for `read_parquet`/`read_csv_auto`, causing a DuckDB binder error.

## Changes

- **`R/last.R`**: Added `get_duckdb_read_opts()` helper that retrieves supported read parameters for a given DuckDB table function on demand by querying the `duckdb_functions()` system catalog. Results are cached in `duckplyr_the` for subsequent calls.

- **`R/compute_parquet.R`**: Uses `intersect(names(options), get_duckdb_read_opts("read_parquet"))` to pass only read-valid options to `read_parquet_duckdb()`.

- **`R/compute_csv.R`**: Uses `intersect(names(options), get_duckdb_read_opts("read_csv_auto"))` to pass only read-valid options to `read_csv_duckdb()`.

- **Tests**: Added test cases for both functions verifying write-only options no longer propagate to the read step.

## Example

```r
df <- data.frame(x = c(1, 2))
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
# Previously errored with: Invalid named parameter "compression_level" for function read_parquet
df <- compute_parquet(df, path, options = list(compression = "zstd", compression_level = 9))
```

Docs: Explain ALTREP deferred string materialization for `collect()` (#724)
description:
Fixes #724

This PR adds a `@details` block to the `collect()` documentation and a note to the `prudence` vignette explaining why calling `str()` on a collected duckplyr dataframe causes a one-time performance hit.

As discussed in the issue, this clarifies for users that duckplyr relies heavily on ALTREP, meaning that string columns defer memory allocation even after `collect()` is called until the values are explicitly accessed. This makes `collect()` extremely fast but pushes the internal materialization cost to the first time the data is read.

title: Fix: Warn instead of error when piping readr output to duckplyr (#694)
description:
Fixes #694

As discussed in the issue, this PR changes the hard error that occurs when piping a `readr` tibble into `as_duckdb_tibble()` into a warning instead, before falling back to automatically casting the result to a standard tibble that duckplyr can read.

This allows users reading CSV files manually with `readr` to still easily proceed into a duckplyr pipeline without unexpected roadblocks, while politely warning them that `read_csv_duckdb()` is the preferred approach for performance.

title: Fix: Filter write-only options in compute_parquet and compute_csv (#886)
description:
Fixes #886

Currently, `compute_parquet` and `compute_csv` crash when given write-specific options like `compression_level` or `force_quote` because duckplyr passes these exact same options to `read_parquet_duckdb` and `read_csv_duckdb`. DuckDB's read functions do not recognize these write options.

This PR adds a filter for known write-only options before the intermediate Parquet/CSV file is read back into DuckDB, fixing the issue. Unit tests have been added to verify this fix for both parquet and csv.

title: feat: Add experimental translation for `filter_out()`
description:
`filter_out()` had no DuckDB backend—always fell back to dplyr. This implements the relational translation so it runs natively in DuckDB.

### Core implementation (`R/filter_out.R`)

The key insight: `filter_out()` keeps rows where NOT ALL conditions are TRUE (i.e., any condition is FALSE or NA). Translated as:

```
NOT (COALESCE(expr1, FALSE) AND COALESCE(expr2, FALSE) AND ...)
```

`COALESCE(expr, FALSE)` maps NA → FALSE, so `NOT FALSE` → TRUE, correctly preserving NA rows. Falls back to dplyr for empty conditions or `.by` usage, matching `filter()` behavior.

### Tests

- Added `filter_out` entries in `test_extra_arg_map` in `tools/00-funs.R` with conditions: `a == 1`, `a %in% 2:3, g == 2`, `a %in% 2:3 & g == 2`, `a != 2 | g != 2`
- Added corresponding parameterized tests in `tests/testthat/test-as_duckplyr_df.R`
- Removed `"filter and filter_out correctly handle empty data frames (#782)"` from `non_force_only_tests` since it now passes in FORCE mode

### Scaffolding

- Added `filter_out = c(".by")` to `nse_args` in `tools/02-duckplyr_df-methods.R`
- Added `@rdname filter.duckplyr_df` to share documentation

title: Improve NEWS.md release notes for v1.1.99.9900
description:
The `duckplyr 1.1.99.9900` release notes were a flat, unordered dump of commit-level entries. Rewrote them as user-facing release notes.

## Changes

- **Priority ordering**: Features → Bug fixes → Documentation → Chore → CI → Testing
- **Added code examples** for all significant user-facing changes:
  - `read_tbl_duckdb()` – attach a DuckDB file and query a table

title: chore: Clean up argument matching by name
description:
`call_match()` was only applied to a subset of functions, so named/reordered arguments like `sum(na.rm = TRUE, a)` or `grepl(x = col, pattern = "pat")` would fail or produce wrong results for aggregation functions and primitives.

title: feat: Enable translation of `first()`, `last()`, `nth()`, and `mutate(n(), .by = ...)`
description:
`n()` used in `mutate()` with `.by` (or without) would fail in DuckDB with "Aggregates cannot be present in a Project relation!" because `n()` was not in the `known_window` list and thus never wrapped in a window expression.

A secondary complication: DuckDB macro functions (like the `n` macro: `() AS CAST(COUNT(*) AS int32)`) cannot be used as window functions — DuckDB rejects `n() OVER (...)` with "Window function macros must be functions".

## Changes

- **`R/translate.R`**
  - Refactored `known_window` from a character vector to a named list `list(name = c(window_alias, non_window_alias))` for consolidated lookup of both membership and per-context aliases (e.g. `n = c("count_star", "n")`, `first = c("first_value", "first")`)
  - Removed `first`, `last`, `nth`, `sd` from the `aliases` map — now handled by `known_window`
  - Changed aggregate `if` block to `else if` (mutually exclusive with the lag/lead/first/last/nth block)
  - Restructured so all non-window handling is inside the `else` branch of `if (window)`, with a single `relexpr_function(aliased_name, args, order_bys = order_bys)` call
  - Added `record_window = NULL` callback parameter to `rel_translate_lang`; called when `window == TRUE` to record window function usage during translation
  - `rel_translate` tracks `used_window` via the callback and returns it as a `has_window` attribute on the result
  - `desc()` in `order_by` arguments for `lag`, `lead`, `first`, `last`, and `nth` now fails with an informative error referencing [duckdb-r#2074](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-r/issues/2074), replacing the previous numeric-only negation workaround

- **`R/relational-expr.R`** — changed `relexpr_function` default `order_bys = list()` to `order_bys = NULL`; updated `stopifnot` accordingly

- **`R/relational-duckdb.R`** — removed `%||% list()` from `to_duckdb_exprs(x$order_bys)` in both the real and meta code paths

- **`R/mutate.R`**
  - `oo_prep`/`oo_restore` are now called per-dot-iteration and only when the expressions for that iteration actually use window functions (detected via the `has_window` attribute from `rel_translate` as translation proceeds) or when `oo_force()` is globally set
  - Calls `oo_restore_order(rel, force = TRUE)` and `oo_restore_cols(rel, force = TRUE)` directly rather than through a wrapper

- **`tests/testthat/test-prudence.R`** — end-to-end test for `mutate(n(), .by = b)` and `mutate(n())` on stingy frames

- **`tests/testthat/test-translate.R`** — snapshot tests for `n()` translation in window context (with and without partition)

- **`tests/testthat/test-duckdb.R`** — low-level tests for the `has_window` attribute from `rel_translate` and for the conditional `oo_prep` behaviour

- **`tools/00-funs.R`** — added `"d = n()"` and `"d = n(), .by = g"` to the `mutate` test cases; commented out `desc()` in `order_by` test cases for `mutate(lag/lead)` and `summarise(first/last/nth)` with a reference to the upstream issue

title: fix: Preserve row order in `mutate()` when window functions with `order_by` are used without `.by`
description:
When using `lag()`/`lead()` with `order_by = desc(x)` in `mutate()` without a `.by` group, DuckDB returned rows sorted by the window `ORDER BY` expression instead of the original input order, causing a mismatch with dplyr's behavior.

## Root cause

`oo_prep()`/`oo_restore()` (row-number-based order preservation) was gated solely on `.by` groups being present. Without grouping, no row number was injected before the window computation, so DuckDB's output order was determined by the window `ORDER BY`.

## Fix

- **`R/mutate.R`**: Extend the `oo_prep()`/`oo_restore()` condition to `length(by_names) > 0 || oo_force()`, so order is preserved whenever `DUCKPLYR_OUTPUT_ORDER = TRUE` (the test default), regardless of grouping.

```r
# Before — output rows sorted by desc(a) instead of input order
test_df %>% as_duckplyr_df_impl() %>% mutate(lag(a, order_by = desc(a)))
#   a g  lag(a, order_by = desc(a))
# 1 6 3                          NA   ← wrong row order
# 2 5 3                           6
# ...

# After — row order matches dplyr
#   a g  lag(a, order_by = desc(a))
# 1 1 1                           2   ← correct
# 2 2 2                           3
# ...
```

title: feat: Reenable translation of `first()`, `last()`, and `nth()` with `desc()` support in `order_by`

Reactivates DuckDB translation for `first()`, `last()`, `nth()`, `lag()`, and `lead()` with full `desc()` support in `order_by` arguments. Fixes pre-existing aggregate context failures caused by `first_value`/`last_value` not existing as aggregate functions in DuckDB 1.4.x.

## Core changes

- **`desc()` in `order_by`**: Detects `desc()` via `is_desc()` and translates to negation (`-x`) in the window ORDER BY expression, since DuckDB's relational API has no native DESC direction for window ORDER BY
- **Aggregate context (`summarise`)**: Uses DuckDB's `first`/`last` aggregates directly (not `first_value`/`last_value` which are window-only); passes `order_bys` into the aggregate call for ordered variants
- **`nth()` in aggregate context**: Translates to `array_extract(list(x ORDER BY ...), n)` 
- **`relexpr_function`**: Added `order_bys` parameter to support aggregate-internal ORDER BY (e.g., `first(a ORDER BY b)`)

## Example

```r
# Now translated to DuckDB (previously fell back to dplyr or errored)
df |> summarise(first(a, order_by = desc(a)), .by = g)
df |> summarise(nth(a, 2, order_by = desc(a)), .by = g)
df |> mutate(lag(a, order_by = desc(a)), .by = g)
df |> mutate(lead(a, order_by = desc(a)), .by = g)

title: feat: New `read_tbl_duckdb()` to read DuckDB tables
description:
Adds `read_tbl_duckdb()` to read tables from DuckDB database files, addressing the first item in #Column.

## Changes

- **New function `read_tbl_duckdb()`**: Attaches a DuckDB file (read-only) and reads the specified table as a duckplyr frame with lazy evaluation support
- **SQL injection prevention**: Escapes paths (single quotes) and identifiers (double quotes) 
- **Deterministic database aliasing**: Uses `rlang::hash()` on normalized path to avoid re-attaching the same database

## Usage

```r
# Read a table from an external DuckDB file
df <- read_tbl_duckdb("data.duckdb", "my_table")

# Supports schema and prudence options
df <- read_tbl_duckdb("data.duckdb", "my_table", schema = "analytics", prudence = "lavish")

# Works with dplyr pipelines (lazy)
read_tbl_duckdb("data.duckdb", "users") %>%
  filter(active) %>%
  select(id, name)
```

The database remains attached for the session to support lazy evaluation of downstream operations.

title: mutate() now supports the argument .keep = "transmute"
description:
Hi @krlmlr,

This merge request seeks to support the new .keep = "transmute" argument in the mutate, based on the dplyr pull request https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/pull/7038

Below I leave an example comparing transmute with mutate(.keep = "transmute")

```
example <- tibble(
  group = c("a", "a", "b", "b"),
  old = c(1, 2, 3, 4)
)

example <- duckplyr::as_duckplyr_df(example)

# transmute --------------------------------------------------------------------

example %>% transmute(
  group,
  new = old * 2,
  old
)

materializing:
---------------------
--- Relation Tree ---
---------------------
Projection ["group" as group, *("old", 2.0) as new, "old" as old]
r_dataframe_scan(0x7fbd82db4148)

---------------------
-- Result Columns  --
---------------------
- group (VARCHAR)
- new (DOUBLE)
- old (DOUBLE)

# A tibble: 4 × 3
group   new   old
<chr> <dbl> <dbl>
1 a         2     1
2 a         4     2
3 b         6     3
4 b         8     4

# mutate(.keep = "transmute") --------------------------------------------------

example %>% mutate(
  .keep = "transmute",
  group,
  new = old * 2,
  old
) 

materializing:
---------------------
--- Relation Tree ---
---------------------
Projection ["group" as group, "new" as new, "old" as old]
Projection ["group" as group, "old" as old, "new" as new]
Projection ["group" as group, "old" as old, *("old", 2.0) as new]
Projection ["group" as group, "old" as old]
r_dataframe_scan(0x7fbd6485f588)

---------------------
-- Result Columns  --
---------------------
- group (VARCHAR)
- new (DOUBLE)
- old (DOUBLE)

# A tibble: 4 × 3
group   new   old
<chr> <dbl> <dbl>
1 a         2     1
2 a         4     2
3 b         6     3
4 b         8     4
```

Regards,

Closes #233. The ability to specify column types by name already exists but was undocumented—only positional syntax was shown.

### Changes
- Added documentation examples showing named column type syntax in `read_csv_duckdb()` and deprecated `df_from_file()`
- Added tests for both positional and named column type specification

### Usage
```r
# Positional (existing docs)
read_csv_duckdb(path, options = list(types = list(c("DOUBLE", "VARCHAR"))))

# By name (new docs)
read_csv_duckdb(path, options = list(types = list(c(a = "DOUBLE", b = "VARCHAR"))))
```

The key insight: named types require a named character vector wrapped in `list()`, which DuckDB interprets as a STRUCT.

title: docs: Document `row.names` incompatibility
description:
DuckDB does not support data frames with row names. When converting via `as_duckdb_tibble()`, row names are silently stripped, which can cause unexpected data loss for users working with data frames like `mtcars`.

Adds a "Row names" subsection to the "Known incompatibilities" section in `vignettes/limits.Rmd`:

- Documents that row names are silently stripped during conversion
- Provides a workaround using `tibble::rownames_to_column()`

```r
# Row names are lost
mtcars |>
  duckplyr::as_duckdb_tibble() |>
  head()

# Workaround: convert to column first
mtcars |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("name") |>
  duckplyr::as_duckdb_tibble() |>
  head()
```

description:
Joint work with @lionel- 

This PR adds partial support for inlining of `across()` in `mutate()` and `summarise()`. If we can successfully inline the `across()` call, then we don't have to fall back to a dplyr implementation.

It currently has the following restrictions:

- You can select multiple `cols`, i.e. `across(c(a, b),)`

- But you can only supply 1 function, i.e. `across(cols, fn)`
    - You cannot do `across(cols, list(fn1 = fn1, fn2 = fn2))`
    - You cannot even do `across(cols, list(fn = fn))`

- Inlined lambdas can be expanded like `across(cols, \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))`
    - But they can't be stored in a variable first, like `fn <- \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)` followed by `across(cols, fn)` 

- Using `.names` is supported, but not particularly useful right now with just 1 function

- Using `.unpack` forces a fallback (like dplyr)

- Using the `...` forces a fallback (like dplyr)

In the future on the dplyr side we'd like to fully deprecate the usage of `...` in `across()`, which currently accepts extra arguments for the `.fns` and is very confusing. After it is deprecated fully we can instead allow it to accept multiple functions, rather than using a list, so you can do: `across(cols, mean, median, \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))`. This is when duckplyr could more easily start accepting >1 functions.

In the details section below, there are a number of examples about when we do vs don't expand.

<details>

``` r
Sys.setenv(DUCKPLYR_FALLBACK_COLLECT = 0)
library(duckplyr)
library(dplyr)

df <- tibble(x = 1:5, y = 6:10)
df <- as_duckplyr_df(df)

# yay both of these work
mutate(df, across(x:y, mean))
#> materializing:
#> ---------------------
#> --- Relation Tree ---
#> ---------------------
#> Projection [mean(x) OVER () as x, mean(y) OVER () as y]
#>   r_dataframe_scan(0x11330e9c8)
#> 
#> ---------------------
#> -- Result Columns  --
#> ---------------------
#> - x (DOUBLE)
#> - y (DOUBLE)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>       x     y
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     3     8
#> 2     3     8
#> 3     3     8
#> 4     3     8
#> 5     3     8

mutate(df, across(x:y, \(arg) mean(arg)))
#> materializing:
#> ---------------------
#> --- Relation Tree ---
#> ---------------------
#> Projection [mean(x) OVER () as x, mean(y) OVER () as y]
#>   r_dataframe_scan(0x114daab48)
#> 
#> ---------------------
#> -- Result Columns  --
#> ---------------------
#> - x (DOUBLE)
#> - y (DOUBLE)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>       x     y
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     3     8
#> 2     3     8
#> 3     3     8
#> 4     3     8
#> 5     3     8

# cool (x_mean as new name)
mutate(df, across(c(x_mean = x, y_mean = y), \(arg) mean(arg)))
#> materializing:
#> ---------------------
#> --- Relation Tree ---
#> ---------------------
#> Projection [x as x, y as y, mean(x) OVER () as x_mean, mean(y) OVER () as y_mean]
#>   r_dataframe_scan(0x112346ec8)
#> 
#> ---------------------
#> -- Result Columns  --
#> ---------------------
#> - x (INTEGER)
#> - y (INTEGER)
#> - x_mean (DOUBLE)
#> - y_mean (DOUBLE)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>       x     y x_mean y_mean
#>   <int> <int>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1     1     6      3      8
#> 2     2     7      3      8
#> 3     3     8      3      8
#> 4     4     9      3      8
#> 5     5    10      3      8

# yep, that's right (x_mean_1 as new name)
mutate(df, across(c(x_mean = x, y_mean = y), \(arg) mean(arg), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"))
#> materializing:
#> ---------------------
#> --- Relation Tree ---
#> ---------------------
#> Projection [x as x, y as y, mean(x) OVER () as x_mean_1, mean(y) OVER () as y_mean_1]
#>   r_dataframe_scan(0x112532708)
#> 
#> ---------------------
#> -- Result Columns  --
#> ---------------------
#> - x (INTEGER)
#> - y (INTEGER)
#> - x_mean_1 (DOUBLE)
#> - y_mean_1 (DOUBLE)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>       x     y x_mean_1 y_mean_1
#>   <int> <int>    <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1     1     6        3        8
#> 2     2     7        3        8
#> 3     3     8        3        8
#> 4     4     9        3        8
#> 5     5    10        3        8

# this falls back due to `.unpack`
mutate(df, across(x:y, \(arg) mean(arg), .unpack = TRUE))
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>       x     y
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     3     8
#> 2     3     8
#> 3     3     8
#> 4     3     8
#> 5     3     8

# this triggers the fallback because it cant translate `na.rm`
mutate(df, across(x:y, \(arg) mean(arg, na.rm = TRUE)))
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>       x     y
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     3     8
#> 2     3     8
#> 3     3     8
#> 4     3     8
#> 5     3     8

# updates from the `a` expression are usable and no fallback is triggered
mutate(df, a = y, across(c(a, x), function(col) col + 1))
#> materializing:
#> ---------------------
#> --- Relation Tree ---
#> ---------------------
#> Projection ["+"(x, 1.0) as x, y as y, "+"(a, 1.0) as a]
#>   Projection [x as x, y as y, y as a]
#>     r_dataframe_scan(0x10725d948)
#> 
#> ---------------------
#> -- Result Columns  --
#> ---------------------
#> - x (DOUBLE)
#> - y (INTEGER)
#> - a (DOUBLE)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>       x     y     a
#>   <dbl> <int> <dbl>
#> 1     2     6     7
#> 2     3     7     8
#> 3     4     8     9
#> 4     5     9    10
#> 5     6    10    11

# looks like `NULL` triggers the fallback-to-dplyr case, so we don't have to
# worry about that i guess
mutate(df, x = NULL)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 1
#>       y
#>   <int>
#> 1     6
#> 2     7
#> 3     8
#> 4     9
#> 5    10

# Not expanded - `list()` not supported even with 1 fn
mutate(df, across(x:y, list(mean = mean)))
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>       x     y x_mean y_mean
#>   <int> <int>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1     1     6      3      8
#> 2     2     7      3      8
#> 3     3     8      3      8
#> 4     4     9      3      8
#> 5     5    10      3      8

# Not expanded - falls back to dplyr
mutate(df, across(x:y, list(mean = mean, median = median)))
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>       x     y x_mean x_median y_mean y_median
#>   <int> <int>  <dbl>    <int>  <dbl>    <int>
#> 1     1     6      3        3      8        8
#> 2     2     7      3        3      8        8
#> 3     3     8      3        3      8        8
#> 4     4     9      3        3      8        8
#> 5     5    10      3        3      8        8

# Not expanded - falls back to dplyr
mutate(df, packed = across(x:y, mean))
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>       x     y packed$x    $y
#>   <int> <int>    <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1     6        3     8
#> 2     2     7        3     8
#> 3     3     8        3     8
#> 4     4     9        3     8
#> 5     5    10        3     8

# Expanded - then falls back to dplyr after duckplyr checks if `mean()`
# matches `base::mean()`
mean <- function(...) stop("oh no")
mutate(df, across(x:y, mean))
#> Error in `mutate()`:
#> ℹ In argument: `across(x:y, mean)`.
#> Caused by error in `across()`:
#> ! Can't compute column `x`.
#> Caused by error:
#> ! oh no
rm(mean)

# All expressions generated by `across()` need to evaluate within the
# same projection (this should return 2s in all columns)
df <- tibble(x = 1, y = 2, z = 3)
df <- as_duckplyr_df(df)
mutate(df, across(x:z, ~ 1 + x))
#> materializing:
#> ---------------------
#> --- Relation Tree ---
#> ---------------------
#> Projection ["+"(1.0, x) as x, "+"(1.0, x) as y, "+"(1.0, x) as z]
#>   r_dataframe_scan(0x112572b48)
#> 
#> ---------------------
#> -- Result Columns  --
#> ---------------------
#> - x (DOUBLE)
#> - y (DOUBLE)
#> - z (DOUBLE)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>       x     y     z
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     2     2     2
```

</details>

---

Some rationale for why we got here:

## Why can't we inline across() in dplyr's generics directly?

Method dispatch makes this hard, S3 signatures currently look like this:

```r
mutate <- function(.data, ...) {
  UseMethod("mutate")
}

mutate.data.frame <- function(.data, ..., .keep, .more) {
  ...
}

mutate.method <- function(.data, ..., .keep, .method_specific) {
  ...
}
```

We could try something like:

```r
mutate <- function(.data, ...) {
  dots <- across_expand(enquos(...))
  mutate_dispatch(.data, !!!dots)
}
mutate_dispatch <- function(.data, ...) {
  UseMethod("mutate")
}
```

But how do we know to not apply `across_expand()` to `.method_specific`? It gets captured in the `...` of the generic when the user calls something like:

```r
mutate(df, across(), .method_specific = "first")
```

We would end up transforming _all_ incoming arguments to quosures, even things like `.keep` that are not meant to be evaluated with `eval_tidy()`.

## So why not export `dplyr::partial_across_expand()` for methods to call manually?

We could try and make the following approach work:

```r
mutate <- function(.data, ...) {
  UseMethod("mutate")
}

mutate.data.frame <- function(.data, ..., .keep, .more) {
  # dplyr specific expanding, fully featured `across_expand()`
}

mutate.method <- function(.data, ..., .keep, .method_specific) {
  # Alternative to `dots <- enquos(...)`
  dots <- dplyr::partial_across_expand(...)
}
```

This gets around the `...` problem from above, because we've matched the dots to the specific S3 method at this point. But there are a number of reasons we don't necessarily want to do this right now:
- We aren't sure how fully featured we can make "partial" expansion while still doing something all backends support. dbplyr and dtplyr already have their own `across()` support, so it is also possible our "partial" support might not capture all the use cases they already support - in which case they'd still need their own version.
- The returned `dots` would likely be `"dplyr_quosures"` which are currently internal dplyr details that we are free to change.
- dplyr itself would not use this, because it would have full across expansion support instead, which unfortunately relies on many internal dplyr details that we would not want to try and expose in any way

Since we don't have enough experience with this new variant yet, we currently want duckplyr to be the only consumer for now. We can revisit exporting it from dplyr once we get a little experience with it and do a cross comparison between duckplyr, dbplyr, and dtplyr to see if we can find some common utility that everyone can happily use.

title: docs: New `fallback_sitrep()` and related functionality for collecting telemetry data
description:
Collection and uploading of fallback events are now a two-step process. At run time, events are written to an `.ndjson` file, one line per entry, one file per process, anonymized. All entries can be reviewed with the new `fallback_review()` and deleted with `fallback_purge()` . The new `fallback_upload()` then uploads the collected data. Uploading can also happen during package load (opt-in).

The new `fallback_sitrep()` gives a situation report about the configuration and the available reports.

Closes #102.

description:
Don't merge until https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/7823 is merged.

DuckDB relational api now exposes all table functions so if the user can specify the function and options that might be nicer. Then we don't have to update dplyr every time duckdb adds a new table function.

the query `from duckdb_functions()  where function_type like '%table%' and (function_name like '%read%' or function_name like '%scan%');` in duckdb shows that there are a number of functions that could be used to read different file formats, (namely json, csv, parquet).

Open to different ideas/implementations for this.

title: Update scripts to run out of the box
description:
Now that duckdb 0.8.0 has been released. Many of the benchmarking and comparison scripts can be updated to run out of the box (once all dependencies are installed). 

This PR increases the tolerance for the compare scripts since the parallel scans of data frames results in a small loss of precision. I imagine 4e-12 is still acceptable. 

Many of the scripts change the name of the queries from `tpch_XX` to `qXX`. This is so that when the queries are graphed, we don't display `tpch_XX` for every query. It's just a small change.

Added a `load-compare-bench.R` script so that the user can execute one command to see the results.
